title: First We Painted
can_do: 用 first/then 讲今天两个连续事件，回答细节追问并补充一个具体画面。
trigger: Dad asks about school, and Child recounts two events in order — painting a big sun and hunting for bugs outside.
setting: A relaxed after-school conversation at home, with Dad and Child seated facing each other.

turns.speaker: child
turns.line: It was good. First we painted a big sun, and then we played outside.

turns.speaker: dad
turns.line: What did you paint the sun with?

turns.speaker: child
turns.line: I used yellow and orange, so it looked really bright.

turns.speaker: child
turns.line: We looked for bugs. I found a small one under a leaf.

turns.speaker: dad
turns.line: A bug hunter! Tell me again at dinner.

replay_cards.title: Paint, then water
replay_cards.setting: A chat with Mom after a garden activity
replay_cards.change: Mom accidentally reverses painting a plant pot and watering the flowers
replay_cards.challenge: Child tells Mom, "First we painted a pot, then we watered flowers." Mom restates the watering first. Child repairs the order with "No, we painted first." Mom acknowledges the corrected sequence. Child adds one detail, "My pot is blue." Mom accepts the account without asking for every garden activity.

replay_cards.title: Remembering our rolls
replay_cards.setting: Talking with Dad after baking together
replay_cards.change: Child remembers mixing but wants a cue for what followed
replay_cards.challenge: Child says he mixed dough with Dad, then asks, "Can you help me remember?" Dad offers one shared cue about the oven. Child continues, "First we mixed, then we baked." He adds, "The rolls were round." Dad restates those two events and Child confirms. Give a cue only when needed; no baking reenactment or third event is required.

parent_support: Accept his first event before inviting the next. First and then can be separate short answers; he does not need to deliver a memorized two-clause sentence.

Ask one genuine detail question about each event — what he painted with, what happened outside. Dad's playful closing shows he listened; it is not a request for Child to repeat the account or prove the order again.
Keep the sun and the bug in the spoken memory. Small empty-hand gestures and a nod are enough. Fetching artwork, painting, bug hunting and a whole-day recap are not part of this conversation.
